title: Sparse table & RMQ (idempotent range queries, LCA via RMQ)
relevance: Medium — static min/max/GCD queries are the “no updates” twin of Fenwick/segtree in OAs; writing an O(1) RMQ template is a common CF Div2 D skill. LCA-via-Euler+RMQ is mostly a rating stretch (binary lifting alone covers most interviews).
company_notes: Many range min/max queries on an immutable array → CSES Static RMQ / NumArray-without-updates; interviewers accept sparse table or segtree, sparse is sharper. Range GCD/AND after preprocessing → 2050F / 1547F shape, sometimes “largest modulus where all equal.” First index where running GCD becomes 1 / array stabilizes under neighbor GCD → 1632D / 1547F. Lowest common manager / org-chart distance with 10^5 queries → CSES Company/Distance Queries; Euler+RMQ OK if the reduction is explained.

phases.goal: Map static idempotent range aggregates and huge-q LCA/distance wording to sparse table (not prefix or Fenwick/segtree).

must_hit.point: Array never changes and many range aggregates of an idempotent op (min, max, GCD, AND, OR, LCM) → sparse table.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names static array + idempotent op family and reaches for sparse table, not a general segtree-first answer.

must_hit.point: Signal words: static array, n,q≤2·10^5, range min/max/GCD, “no modifications,” binary search + range check, tree distance / lowest common ancestor with huge q.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those signals and ties them to ST / RMQ rather than naive scans.

must_hit.point: Do not use the two-block trick for sum/XOR (use prefix); if updates appear, switch to Fenwick/segtree.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates sum/XOR→prefix and updates→Fenwick/segtree from static idempotent→ST.

must_hit.point: “Many range minimum / maximum queries, array immutable” or “lowest common manager / distance in org chart with 10^5 queries” are core OA/interview shapes for sparse RMQ / Euler+RMQ.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names immutable RMQ or org-chart LCA/distance and prefers sparse (or Euler+RMQ) as the sharp answer.

probes: Static range min vs static range sum vs point updates—what structure do you pick, and why?
What wording makes you reach for sparse table instead of prefix or Fenwick/segtree?

hints.1: Ask whether the array changes and whether the op is idempotent (min/max/GCD/…) or sum/XOR.
hints.2: Static idempotent → sparse; static sum/XOR → prefix; updates → Fenwick/segtree; huge-q LCA/distance can be Euler+RMQ.
hints.3: Say: immutable min/max/GCD/AND/OR/LCM ranges → sparse table; sum/XOR → prefix; updates → Fenwick/segtree; signals include static array, n,q≤2·10^5, no modifications, BS+range check, org-chart LCA with 10^5 queries.

phases.goal: State the sparse-table covering idea, when overlap is legal, and the Euler-tour RMQ reduction for LCA.

must_hit.point: Precompute st[k][i] = op on [i, i+2^k), then answer [L,R] with two overlapping blocks of length 2^⌊log2(R−L+1)⌋.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes power-of-two table layers and the two-block query cover.

must_hit.point: Overlap is legal exactly because op(x,x)=x (idempotence); that is why the two-block trick fails for sum/XOR.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties overlapping blocks to idempotence and contrasts sum/XOR.

must_hit.point: LCA via RMQ: Euler tour of nodes + depth array + first[v]; LCA(u,v)=euler[rmq_argmin(first[u], first[v])] — argmin depth between first occurrences.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States Euler + first occurrences + argmin on depths for LCA.

must_hit.point: Binary search + ST check for monotone length/threshold/shots predicates (1709D, 514D, 1547F); prefer ST LCA when q is huge or Euler already exists (else binary lifting is equivalent).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions BS+ST check patterns and when Euler+RMQ is preferred over binlift.

probes: How do you answer a range min with a sparse table in constant query time?
How does Euler tour + RMQ turn LCA into an array RMQ?

hints.1: Think power-of-two blocks and when overlapping ranges are safe.
hints.2: Build st[k][i] on [i,i+2^k); query with two blocks of length 2^⌊log2(len)⌋; LCA = argmin depth on Euler between first[u], first[v].
hints.3: Say: st[k][i]=op on [i,i+2^k); query op of two overlapping 2^k blocks because op(x,x)=x; not for sum/XOR; LCA via Euler+depths+first then euler[rmq_argmin(...)]; BS+ST for monotone checks; ST when q huge / Euler ready.

phases.goal: Code sparse-table build/query (and optional Euler+RMQ LCA) with consistent indexing and log precompute.

must_hit.point: Build: st[0][i]=a[i]; st[k][i]=op(st[k-1][i], st[k-1][i+2^{k-1}]) for all i+2^k≤n.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes the layer-0 init and the doubling recurrence with the i+2^k≤n bound.

must_hit.point: Query [L,R]: k=floor(log2(R-L+1)); op(st[k][L], st[k][R-2^k+1]). Precompute lg[] or use __builtin_clz.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States that exact k and two-index query, plus lg/clz.

must_hit.point: LCA via RMQ: Euler tour of nodes + depth array + first[v]; LCA(u,v)=euler[rmq_argmin(first[u], first[v])].
must_hit.evidence_hint: Implements or narrates first[], Euler, depth RMQ argmin, then map back via euler[].

must_hit.point: Indexing: be consistent 0- vs 1-based; empty range / L>R guard; long long when combining values, int fine for indices.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out base consistency, L>R guard, and long long for combined values.

probes: Write the sparse-table build recurrence and the two-block query formula.
How do you wire Euler tour, first[], and argmin RMQ for LCA?

hints.1: Start from st[0], then doubling layers, then the query k and two indices.
hints.2: st[k][i]=op(st[k-1][i], st[k-1][i+2^{k-1}]); k=floor(log2(R-L+1)); op(st[k][L], st[k][R-2^k+1]); LCA uses euler[rmq_argmin(first[u],first[v])].
hints.3: Spell: st[0][i]=a[i]; st[k][i]=op(st[k-1][i], st[k-1][i+2^{k-1}]) for i+2^k≤n; query with k=floor(log2(R-L+1)) and op(st[k][L], st[k][R-2^k+1]) via lg[]/__builtin_clz; LCA=euler[rmq_argmin(first[u],first[v])]; guard L>R; long long for values.

phases.goal: Anchor sparse-table preprocess/query costs and the static n,q regimes stated in the topic.

must_hit.point: Sparse table build uses space/time O(n log n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(n log n) preprocess space and time.

must_hit.point: Idempotent two-block RMQ answers in O(1) after preprocessing (including O(1) GCD / O(1) LCA when using ST).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(1) query for the two-block / ST-backed RMQ or LCA.

must_hit.point: Signal / interview scale: static array with n,q≤2·10^5; org-chart distance / LCA with 10^5 queries.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions n,q≤2·10^5 static RMQ signals and 10^5 LCA/distance queries.

probes: What are the preprocess and query costs of a sparse table?
What n,q scales does the topic treat as the usual static-RMQ / LCA interview regime?

hints.1: Separate build cost from per-query cost, then name the stated constraints.
hints.2: Build O(n log n); query O(1) via two blocks; typical signals n,q≤2·10^5 or 10^5 LCA queries.
hints.3: Say: space/time O(n log n) to build; O(1) two-block query for idempotent ops; static RMQ often signaled with n,q≤2·10^5; org-chart LCA/distance with 10^5 queries.

phases.goal: Catch non-idempotent two-block misuse, rebuild-under-updates, and indexing/empty-range bugs.

must_hit.point: Using the two-block sparse query for sum/XOR — overlap double-counts; use prefix instead.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects two-block ST for sum/XOR and names prefix.

must_hit.point: Rebuilding the sparse table per query, or keeping ST when point/range updates appear — switch to Fenwick/segtree.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists ST is static preprocess once; updates force Fenwick/segtree.

must_hit.point: Inconsistent 0- vs 1-based indexing, or missing empty-range / L>R guards on queries.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Flags base mismatch and L>R / empty range handling.

must_hit.point: Forgetting long long when combining values (int is fine for indices only).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses long long for combined ST values while keeping int indices.

probes: What goes wrong if you answer a range sum with the two overlapping sparse blocks?
Which bugs show up first: updates on an ST, indexing, or empty ranges?

hints.1: Check op idempotence, update model, and index/empty-range hygiene.
hints.2: Sum/XOR → prefix not two-block; never rebuild ST under updates—use Fenwick/segtree; consistent bases; guard L>R; long long for values.
hints.3: Say: two-block only if op(x,x)=x—sum/XOR need prefix; no updates→sparse, updates→Fenwick/segtree, never rebuild ST per query; consistent 0/1-based with L>R guard; long long for combined values.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: No updates and an idempotent op → sparse table; point/range updates → Fenwick/segtree. Never rebuild ST per query.

tradeoffs.topic: Two-block sparse query vs prefix sums
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Idempotent ops (min, max, GCD, AND, OR, LCM) may use two overlapping power-of-two blocks because op(x,x)=x. Sum/XOR must not—use prefix (or a disjoint sparse table as stretch).

Same RMQ on an Euler tour of depths turns LCA into argmin depth between first occurrences; equivalent to binary lifting. Prefer ST when q is huge or you already have Euler; binary lifting alone covers most interviews.

tradeoffs.topic: Tree path aggregates: lift vs Euler/HLD/segtree
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Distance via depths (dep[u]+dep[v]-2·dep[lca]); max/GCD on path → lift with stored op, or Euler+HLD/segtree (609E / Ant colony style).

gotchas.trap: Answering range sum or XOR with the two overlapping sparse-table blocks.
gotchas.correction: Overlap is legal only for idempotent ops; for sum/XOR use prefix (not the two-block trick).

gotchas.trap: Using a sparse table when the array must support updates, or rebuilding ST every query.
gotchas.correction: Static only: preprocess once; if updates appear, switch to Fenwick/segtree.

gotchas.trap: Mixing 0- and 1-based indices or querying when L>R / the range is empty.
gotchas.correction: Pick one indexing convention and stick to it; guard empty ranges / L>R; int is fine for indices.

gotchas.trap: Combining ST values in int on problems where aggregates can overflow.
gotchas.correction: Use long long when combining values; int remains fine for indices.

gotchas.trap: Treating LCA-via-Euler+RMQ as mandatory in interviews.
gotchas.correction: It is mostly a rating stretch; binary lifting alone covers most interviews, though Euler+RMQ is acceptable if you can explain the reduction.
